steps.title: Create the Profile component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Profile that accepts a prop called 'user' of type User. The component should return a simple JSX structure.
steps.hint: Define a function or arrow function named Profile that takes props with a 'user' property typed as User. Return a JSX element like a div.
steps.expectedOutcome: A Profile component is created with the correct prop typing and returns JSX.
successCriteria: The Profile component should be defined as a function or arrow function, accept a 'user' prop of type User, and return a JSX element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Profile component with the correct prop typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the Profile component accepts a 'user' prop of type User and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Profile component is not defined correctly. Ensure it's a function that accepts a 'user' prop of type User and returns JSX.

steps.title: Define the withAuth HOC function signature
steps.instruction: Define a higher-order component function named 'withAuth' that takes a component as its parameter and returns a new component. Use TypeScript generics to type the component props.
steps.hint: Start by writing 'function withAuth' or 'const withAuth =' and define the function signature with a generic type parameter for the component props.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'withAuth' is defined with proper TypeScript typing for the component parameter and return value.
successCriteria: Function named 'withAuth' exists
Function takes a component parameter typed with ComponentType
Function returns a new component
Uses TypeScript generics for props typing
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly defined the withAuth HOC function signature with proper TypeScript typing. This establishes the foundation for adding authentication logic in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: 1) Is the function named 'withAuth'? 2) Does it take a component parameter with proper typing? 3) Does it return a new component? 4) Are you using TypeScript generics for the props?
steps.feedbackWrong:
The withAuth function signature isn't quite right. Remember to: 1) Create a function named 'withAuth' 2) Accept a component parameter typed as ComponentType

3) Return a new component function 4) Use TypeScript generics

for the props type.

steps.title: Add authentication check logic to withAuth
steps.instruction: Inside the withAuth HOC function, add logic that checks if the user is authenticated and conditionally renders the wrapped component or a fallback message.
steps.hint: Use a conditional (if statement or ternary) to check user.isAuthenticated. Return the wrapped component if true, otherwise return a fallback JSX element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The withAuth HOC now contains conditional rendering logic that checks authentication status and returns appropriate JSX.
successCriteria: The withAuth function should include a conditional check (if statement or ternary) that returns the wrapped component when authenticated and a fallback JSX element when not authenticated.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the authentication check logic to the withAuth HOC. The conditional rendering will show different content based on the user's authentication status.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the authentication logic needs more work. Make sure you're checking user.isAuthenticated and returning the wrapped component when true, and a fallback JSX element when false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The authentication check logic is missing or incorrect. The withAuth HOC should contain conditional rendering that checks if the user is authenticated and returns appropriate JSX based on that condition.

steps.title: Create mock user data
steps.instruction: Create a mockUser object that implements the User interface. Set its id to 1, name to 'John Doe', and email to 'john@example.com'.
steps.hint: Define a constant variable named mockUser and assign it an object with the required properties matching the User interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A mockUser constant is created with the correct properties and values.
successCriteria: The code includes a mockUser constant that matches the User interface with id: 1, name: 'John Doe', and email: 'john@example.com'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created mock user data that implements the User interface. This will be useful for testing our components.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your mockUser object has all three required properties (id, name, email) with the correct values and types.
steps.feedbackWrong: The mockUser object doesn't match the requirements. Make sure it implements the User interface with id: 1, name: 'John Doe', and email: 'john@example.com'.

steps.title: Apply withAuth to Profile component
steps.instruction: Create a new component called AuthenticatedProfile by wrapping the Profile component with the withAuth higher-order component.
steps.hint: Call withAuth(Profile) to create the wrapped component. You can assign it to a const variable or export it directly.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of wrapping a component with a HOC
const AuthenticatedButton = withAuth(Button);
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have an AuthenticatedProfile component that is the Profile component wrapped with the withAuth HOC.
successCriteria: Create AuthenticatedProfile component
Wrap Profile with withAuth
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the AuthenticatedProfile component by wrapping Profile with the withAuth HOC.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're wrapping the Profile component with withAuth and naming the result AuthenticatedProfile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The AuthenticatedProfile component wasn't created correctly. Remember to call withAuth(Profile) and assign it to a variable named AuthenticatedProfile.

steps.title: Create the main App component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named App that returns JSX. Inside the component, render the authenticated Profile component (which is the result of applying withAuth to Profile).
steps.hint: Define the App component using either a function declaration or arrow function. Return JSX that includes the authenticated component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component is defined and returns JSX containing the authenticated Profile component.
successCriteria: App component is defined
Returns JSX
Includes the authenticated Profile component in the JSX
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the main App component that will render the authenticated Profile component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the App component, but it's missing either the JSX return or the authenticated Profile component. Make sure to include both.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component is not properly defined. Ensure you create a functional component named App that returns JSX containing the authenticated Profile component.

steps.title: Render AuthenticatedProfile in App
steps.instruction: Inside your App component's JSX, render the AuthenticatedProfile component and pass the mockUser object as a prop.
steps.hint: Add <AuthenticatedProfile user={mockUser} /> inside the return statement of your App component.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now renders the AuthenticatedProfile component with the mockUser data passed as a prop.
successCriteria: The App component's JSX should include <AuthenticatedProfile user={mockUser} /> inside the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully rendered the AuthenticatedProfile component in your App with the mockUser prop. This completes the integration of your HOC-wrapped component into the main application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there's something missing. Make sure you're rendering AuthenticatedProfile with the user prop set to mockUser inside the App component's return statement.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add the AuthenticatedProfile component to your App's JSX and pass the mockUser object as a prop.

steps.title: Test with authenticated user
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, render the AuthenticatedProfile component and pass the mockUser as the user prop to verify the HOC works when authenticated.
steps.hint: Add <AuthenticatedProfile user={mockUser} /> inside the App component's return JSX.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Profile component should render with the mock user's data when the app runs, since isAuthenticated is true in the HOC.
successCriteria: The App component renders AuthenticatedProfile with the mockUser prop.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully rendered the authenticated Profile component with user data. The HOC allows the Profile to show because isAuthenticated is true.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're rendering AuthenticatedProfile (not Profile directly) and passing mockUser as the user prop.
steps.feedbackWrong: The App component doesn't render AuthenticatedProfile with the mockUser prop. Check that you added the component inside the return JSX with the correct prop.

steps.title: Test with unauthenticated user
steps.instruction: In the withAuth HOC, change the isAuthenticated constant from true to false to simulate an unauthenticated user and verify the fallback message appears.
steps.hint: Look for the isAuthenticated variable inside the WithAuthWrapper function and change its value from true to false.
steps.analogousExample:
// Inside a HOC wrapper function
const isAuthenticated = false; // Changed from true to false
steps.expectedOutcome: When isAuthenticated is set to false, the HOC should display the fallback message 'Please log in to view this content.' instead of the Profile component.
successCriteria: Change the value of isAuthenticated from true to false
The fallback message should be displayed when isAuthenticated is false
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully changed the authentication state to false. The HOC now displays the fallback message when the user is not authenticated, demonstrating how the HOC protects content.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you changed the isAuthenticated value from true to false inside the WithAuthWrapper function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isAuthenticated value should be changed to false to test the unauthenticated scenario. Look for the const isAuthenticated = true line inside the WithAuthWrapper function.
